package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware targeting Linux servers, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects Linux servers, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: Erebus ransomware is malicious because it is specifically designed to encrypt files on Linux servers, rendering critical data and services inaccessible. The malware then demands a ransom payment for decryption, directly extorting victims and causing operational disruption and potential data loss.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon execution of the malicious binary)
execution_context.file_location: infected Linux server (typically dropped in /tmp, /var/tmp, or another writable directory)
required_permissions: filesystem (read and write access to files and directories)
process execution (ability to spawn subprocesses for file enumeration and encryption)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: for file in $(find / -type f); do encrypt $file; done
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code recursively enumerates all files on the filesystem, applies an encryption routine to each file, and overwrites the original data, resulting in denial of access to all user and system files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Recursively encrypting every file on the filesystem is a clear indicator of ransomware activity and is never performed by legitimate server processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal server operations do not perform bulk encryption or destructive modification of all files without explicit user initiation and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or migration scripts may read or copy many files, but they do not encrypt or irreversibly alter file contents.
key_indicators: Recursive traversal of the entire filesystem
Bulk application of encryption to user and system files
No user interaction or confirmation required
Overwriting original files with encrypted versions

execution_context.file_location: infected Linux server (ransom note dropped in /root, user home directories, and other prominent locations)
required_permissions: filesystem (write access to root and user directories)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: echo 'Your files have been encrypted. Pay 1 BTC to the following address to recover your data.' > /root/README_FOR_DECRYPT.txt
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after encrypting files, the code writes a ransom note to key directories, instructing the victim to pay a specified amount in cryptocurrency to recover access to their data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creating ransom notes that demand cryptocurrency payment for file recovery is a direct and unambiguous sign of ransomware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software never demands payment for access to user data or creates files instructing users to pay a ransom.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate software creates files demanding payment for data recovery.
key_indicators: Creation of ransom note files in root and user directories
Text content referencing file encryption and payment instructions

attack_chain.action: Malware binary is executed on the Linux server, gaining access to the filesystem and process execution capabilities.
All files on the server are recursively enumerated and encrypted, rendering data and services inaccessible.
Ransom note files are written to disk in root and user directories, instructing the victim to pay a cryptocurrency ransom for decryption.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extortion attempt and potential ransom payment

behavioral_signatures: Rapid, bulk access and modification of files across the entire filesystem within a short time window
Creation of ransom note files (e.g., README_FOR_DECRYPT.txt, FILES_ENCRYPTED.txt) containing payment instructions
Unusual process activity not matching known legitimate software, especially processes performing mass file encryption
file_indicators: User files with new, unusual file extensions appended (e.g., .encrypted, .erebus)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to cryptocurrency-related services or addresses referenced in ransom notes
Possible command-and-control (C2) communication if the malware reports infection status or receives instructions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that rapidly enumerate and modify large numbers of files, especially if file extensions change or files become unreadable. Detect the creation of ransom note files in root or user directories containing cryptocurrency payment instructions. Correlate with any unusual outbound network activity, particularly connections to cryptocurrency services or domains mentioned in ransom notes. Alert on any process that writes files with ransom demands or exhibits mass file encryption behavior.
